definitions.gloss: keyboard; keys (of a piano or organ)
definitions.explanation: The set of keys on a musical instrument such as a piano, organ, or synthesizer. Also used to refer to keyboard instruments in general.

examples.japanese: ⟦ピアノ→ピアノ：01376_piano⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{鍵盤|けんばん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{触|ふ}れた→触れる：01984_fureru⟧。
⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{電子|でんし}→電子：03449_denshi⟧⟦ピアノ→ピアノ：01376_piano⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧88{鍵盤|けんばん}⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{頃|ころ}、⟦{音楽|おんがく}→音楽：00661_ongaku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{授業|じゅぎょう}→授業：00781_jugyou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{鍵盤|けんばん}ハーモニカ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{吹|ふ}いた→吹く：02445_fuku⟧。
examples.english: As a child, I played the melodica in music class.

notes:
Primarily refers to musical instrument keys, not computer keyboards (which are ⟦キーボード→キーボード：04410_kiiboodo⟧). However, {鍵盤|けんばん} can sometimes refer to a keyboard instrument itself in casual speech.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鍵盤|けんばん}⟦{楽器|がっき}→楽器：13159_gakki⟧ (keyboard instrument)
- {鍵盤|けんばん}ハーモニカ (melodica — standard in Japanese elementary school music education)
- 88{鍵盤|けんばん} (88 keys — full piano)
- {白|しろ}{鍵|けん} / {黒|くろ}{鍵|けん} (white key / black key — individual keys)

The {鍵盤|けんばん}ハーモニカ is a ubiquitous part of Japanese elementary education. Nearly every Japanese person has played one in school.
